Our todo CLI needs tags. This is what I would like:

- `todo add` takes `--tag TAG`, and it can be given more than once. Tags are kept in
  lower case, without repeats, in a `tags` list on the item in the todo file. A tag may
  use letters, digits, and hyphens only and starts with a letter or digit; anything else
  should be a bad command line (exit status 2 with a message, and nothing added).
  `todo list` should show an item's tags after its title (and its due day) as `#tag`.
- `todo list --tag TAG` shows only the items that have that tag, ignoring case. Giving
  `--tag` more than once keeps only the items that have every one of the tags.
- `todo list --sort KEY` orders the list. `title` is alphabetical and ignores case, and
  `due` puts the earliest due day first with items that have no due day last. Ties go by
  item number. An unknown key is a bad command line.
- `todo list --sort tag` orders the list by the team's tag priority in
  data/tag-order.json, highest priority first. An item is ranked by its highest priority
  tag, items with no tag that the file lists come last, and ties go by item number.

Items without tags and the commands we have now should keep working and printing as they
do today.
